title: TS-23 Tasks
description:
## Slice 2 ticket 23 of 40, phase notes: paths use `conversation/` (the workspace as it is on develop). Design source: `git show origin/docs/typescript-control-plane:docs/TYPESCRIPT_CONTROL_PLANE.md` (section 8, row 23); read sections 0.3, 2, 3 and 6 as needed. Read AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING_AGENT.md first. Never read or write `project/`; use `kbs` only.

## Goal
Port tasks: the task domain, the Pi tool `task`, and the task routes. Registering a Pi tool needs verified API code.

## Kind
prototype-first: a library API in this ticket is uncertain. A Sonnet agent must FIRST produce verified, runnable code for it (see Prototype section), paste it into this ticket as a comment, and ONLY THEN is the ticket completed with that code verbatim. A Haiku implementer must not start the build part until that comment exists; if it is missing, stop and report.

## Branch and commit
```text
git fetch origin
git switch -c ts/23-tasks origin/develop
...work, then...
git add <only the files listed under Files>
git commit -m "feat(conversation): tasks

Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"
git push -u origin ts/23-tasks
```
Do NOT open a pull request; the orchestrator opens it. Commit messages contain no emojis.

## Files to create or change
- `conversation/src/domain/tasks.ts`
- `conversation/src/pi/task-tool.ts`
- `conversation/src/http/routes/tasks.ts`
- `conversation/features-support/steps/task.steps.ts`

## Exported interface and error behavior
Routes `GET/POST /api/orgs/{tenant}/users/{u}/tasks`, `GET/PATCH /tasks/{id}` with the Python status codes. Tool name `task` with the same JSON schema as the Python tool definition (find it with `grep -n "task" python/src/chatticus/thin_task.py`).

General rules: TypeScript ESM, `.ts` import suffixes as in conversation/src/storage/; tabs for indentation as in existing files; long clear names; no line comments; TSDoc on exported symbols; no emojis. Each Python exception class used by a ported function becomes an exported `Error` subclass with the same name and the same message text. Failures are thrown, never returned as magic values, unless the Python returned them.

## Python source to port (keep structure; read it fully before writing)
- `python/src/chatticus/thin_task.py (217 lines)`
- `python/src/chatticus/control_plane.py lines 876-1008`
Rule: mechanical ports keep the Python file's structure and cite the Python line range in the commit body. Behavior that no scenario encodes is still kept.

## Prototype (must be done and pasted before the build)
Re-use the ticket 18 prototype for tool registration; if absent for tools, a Sonnet agent proves that a registered tool is called from a scripted provider and its result reaches the transcript.

## Behavior spec (Gherkin, ported unchanged)
Existing features that must pass under cucumber-js when this ticket closes. Do NOT edit these `.feature` files except where this ticket says a behavior changed.

### features/thin_task_item.feature
Scenarios: A bot creates a task from the first readiness gate without summoning a computer; A task cannot reach completed without evidence; A task completes only with system evidence; A task closes with a recorded reason; Tasks are isolated by tenant

completing the task is refused for missing evidence   <-  features/steps/thin_task_item_steps.py:73

### features/web_task_list.feature
Scenarios: The web UI loads the household task list from the same-origin API; The web UI shows an empty state when there are no tasks; The web UI loads task details for a stored task; The web UI handles a missing task gracefully
Step texts to implement in TypeScript (exact step text, then the Python step that implements it today):
```text
an empty control plane   <-  features/steps/control_plane_steps.py:48
tenant "anthus" user "ryan" has a bot named "Assistant"   <-  features/steps/control_plane_steps.py:280
tenant "anthus" posts the task tool create action for bot "Assistant" with title "Pay the electric bill"   <-  features/steps/thin_task_http_steps.py:13
the web UI requests the task list for tenant "anthus" user "ryan"   <-  features/steps/web_task_list_steps.py:10
the web UI task list shows:   <-  features/steps/web_task_list_steps.py:26
the web UI task list is empty   <-  features/steps/web_task_list_steps.py:37
the web UI requests task details for the stored task as tenant "anthus"   <-  features/steps/web_task_list_steps.py:43
the web UI task detail shows title "Pay the electric bill"   <-  features/steps/web_task_list_steps.py:65
the web UI task detail shows status "open"   <-  features/steps/web_task_list_steps.py:71
the web UI requests task "missing-task-id" as tenant "anthus"   <-  features/steps/web_task_list_steps.py:54
the web UI task detail request fails with not found   <-  features/steps/web_task_list_steps.py:77
```
Cucumber expressions: convert each Python `{name}` parse pattern to `{string}`, `{int}` or `{word}` using `npx tsx conversation/bin/convert-step-pattern.ts '<pattern>'` (from ticket 3) and review the output by hand. Step text must not change unless behavior changed. Steps call `this.api` (HTTP via `app.request()`) for HTTP steps and the same domain functions the routes call for direct steps; steps never reach into a store.
Step file(s) to write: under `conversation/features-support/steps/` as named in Files above (at most about 400 lines each; split by subject).

Failing run first (required):
```text
1. Write or port the step file(s) and any new .feature file.
2. cd conversation && npx cucumber-js ../features/<feature>.feature   -> confirm the scenarios FAIL for the right reason (missing production code, not a typo in a step). Save the first failing summary line for the commit body.
3. Write the smallest production code that passes. Re-run until green.
```
Manifest: when EVERY scenario of a feature is covered by this ticket (not marked partial above), add `features/<name>.feature` to `features/ported-features.txt` and add `<name>` to the alternation in `python/behave.ini` `exclude_re` (the manifest vitest `conversation/test/ported-features-manifest.test.ts` fails if they disagree). For a partial feature leave the manifest alone; the ticket named in the note finishes it. To run a partial feature, pass the path and `--name '<scenario>'` to cucumber-js; if CLI paths do not override the config paths, stop and report.

## Dependencies (blocked-by)
- ticket 14 (chatticus-c32c35): Bots, channels and roster; provides what its Files section lists.
- ticket 18 (chatticus-2ffc48): Prototype and build: turn executor core; provides what its Files section lists.

## Verify
```text
cd conversation && npm run typecheck && npm test && npx cucumber-js ../features/<each feature of this ticket>.feature
```
moto setup (copied from the `conversation` job in .github/workflows/ci.yml):
```text
python -m pip install "moto[server]==5.2.3"
nohup moto_server -p 5555 > moto.log 2>&1 &
for i in $(seq 1 30); do if (echo > /dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/5555) 2>/dev/null; then break; fi; sleep 1; done
export CHATTICUS_TEST_AWS_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:5555
```
Install once at the repo root: `npm ci`. Stop moto when done: `pkill -f "moto_server -p 5555"`.
If the ticket added a feature to the manifest also run `cd conversation && npx cucumber-js` (full manifest) and `cd python && behave` is NOT required for ported features, but run `cd python && black --check src ../features tests && ruff check src ../features tests` if you touched anything under python/ or features/steps/.
Final cleanup before pushing:
```text
git status
```
Make sure NO `.orig`, `.rej`, `node_modules`, `build/`, `dist/`, `moto.log`, `.venv` or other stray files are staged: `git diff --cached --name-only | grep -E '\.orig$|\.rej$|node_modules|(^|/)build/|(^|/)dist/|moto\.log|\.venv'` must print nothing.

## Stop rules
If anything in this ticket is wrong, ambiguous, impossible, or contradicted by the code you find (a Python line range does not match, a step has no Python match, a library API differs from what is written, a scenario cannot pass without changing its text), STOP and report to the orchestrator with the exact file, line and observation. Never improvise, never weaken or delete a scenario to make it pass, never add a fallback or a compatibility branch.

## Python to delete
No production Python is deleted by this ticket (the one big deletion is ticket 40). The only deletions allowed: the per-feature step file of each feature newly added to the manifest, because the manifest vitest requires it: features/steps/thin_task_item_steps.py (if it exists), features/steps/thin_task_http_steps.py (if it exists), features/steps/web_task_list_steps.py (if it exists). Shared step files (control_plane_steps.py, capability_policy_steps.py, messaging_steps.py, organization_steps.py and the like) are never edited here; the last ticket that uses them leaves them for ticket 40.
